findings.fix: Wrap the _repo_path.html literals in t ("Choose folder…", "chosen:", "picker failed") and add their German entries to germanCatalog.
findings.claim: On a casual German install the Projekte add form still renders English labels: repos_index.html:7 includes _repo_path.html, whose button reads a raw "Choose folder…", whose chosen-path line reads "chosen:" and whose error badge reads "picker failed" — none go through t and none are in germanCatalog. Spec-5 (correctness-54) requires the casual repos_index to keep the add form with t-localized labels.
findings.evidence: Re-read repos_index.html lines 5-15 at 1f725ce: the casual branch renders the same add form, with {{template "_repo_path.html" .AddPath}} at line 7 and t applied only to name/label placeholders, Add, add, remove, Remove and the confirm text. git show 1f725ce:internal/server/templates/_repo_path.html: line 4 `>Choose folder…</button>`, line 5 `picker failed`, line 6 `chosen: <code>` — all raw literals. i18n.go germanCatalog lines 8-122 hold no key for any of them. Sequence: profile language de + audience casual -> GET /repos -> the button reads 'Choose folder…' next to German 'hinzufügen'/'Hinzufügen'. The partial is an unchanged file, but the requirement sits on the casual add form this diff introduced.

findings.fix: For the casual audience render a plain translated result line (e.g. t "Project added" / the error root cause) instead of the lock-key subject and the raw op output, or at least give handleReposAdd/Delete a human Subject and drop the 'additionalDirectories grant' wording from the casual output.
findings.claim: Every casual project add shows developer/engine text: handleReposAdd goes through runRepoOp(registryLockKey, …), so the op-result card's Subject is the lock key "_registry", the badge is English "Ok"/"Failed", and since casual adds always grant (line 570) the output line is "added <name> (<path>) + additionalDirectories grant" in a terminal window. A Claude settings key and an internal lock name are exactly the developer jargon spec-1/2 (correctness-11, -13) say the casual user never reads.
